investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity or a ready state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are full; if the affinity rules were broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling would succeed.
Tertiary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit set too low at the namespace or node level: the resource ceiling may not reflect actual hardware capacity, causing premature exhaustion.

Quaternary — a surge in concurrent remote agent creation requests (from other users or automated jobs) consumed all VM slots before the eval pod was scheduled, causing transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity ceiling.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity or a ready state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message for 147s, confirming the condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message for 145s, confirming all three remote-agent checks hit the same scheduling wall.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are full; if the affinity rules were broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling would succeed.
Tertiary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit set too low at the namespace or node level: the resource ceiling may not reflect actual hardware capacity, causing premature exhaustion.

Quaternary — a surge in concurrent remote agent creation requests (from other users or automated jobs) consumed all VM slots before the eval pod was scheduled, causing transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity ceiling.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-09 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api had exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 available slots and no preemption victims found, every eval attempt to provision a remote agent pod timed out unscheduled (~129–152 seconds per attempt), preventing any agent lifecycle progress and producing zero evidence output. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is localized to the observability eval environment targeting production-api.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the cluster has consumed all available peer-pod VM slots on the only nodes eligible for remote agent pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts and no preemption victims to displace.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates. If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., due to a prior eval run that did not clean up, a surge in remote agent usage, or node maintenance), the effective schedulable pool drops to zero.

Tertiary — eval cleanup failure leaving orphaned pods: if a prior eval run's withCleanup() did not successfully terminate remote agent pods (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1916), those pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new scheduling.

Lower confidence — node affinity selector change: a configuration change to the pod's node affinity or to node labels could have reduced the matching node pool from more than 2 to exactly 2, shrinking available capacity. No suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A subsequent eval run that succeeds in scheduling a remote agent pod and returns all 5 required evidence fields would disprove that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is currently exhausted.

Cluster node inspection showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the affinity-matching nodes at the time of the failure would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause and point instead to a misconfiguration (e.g., wrong resource name, quota, or admission webhook rejection).

A scheduler event or audit log showing the pod was rejected for a reason other than resource exhaustion (e.g., taint/toleration mismatch, PodSecurityPolicy, or admission webhook) would shift the diagnosis away from capacity exhaustion.

Evidence that the remote-agent-create sibling check passed (or that a remote agent pod was successfully scheduled) during the same time window would disprove that the entire scheduling pool was exhausted and suggest a transient or race condition instead.
Confirmation that no prior eval run left orphaned remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots would weaken the cleanup-failure hypothesis.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks the available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource count on affinity-matching nodes before attempting agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct, early-failing check rather than a timeout buried in the agent provisioning flow.
Add an eval that verifies no orphaned remote-agent pods are present in the cluster after each eval run, confirming that withCleanup() successfully released all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

Add a scheduling-headroom eval that alerts when the ratio of allocated-to-allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on eligible nodes exceeds a warning threshold (e.g., 80%), providing advance notice before full exhaustion causes eval failures.

Consider a post-run cleanup verification step within the remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, and remote-agent-state evals that confirms the provisioned pod was successfully deleted, catching cleanup failures before they accumulate into capacity exhaustion.
